summary:
Space Mission is an interactive engineering simulation web app where players design, builds and flies a multi-stage rocket. Players choose spacecraft modules such as cockpits, payloads, fuel tanks and engines while managing constraints such as mass, thrust-to-weight ratio, delta-v, power, communications, science objectives and budget.

Players can attempt missions ranging from Low Earth Orbit and geostationary orbit to lunar orbit and a Moon landing, where scientific data can be collected. Real-time telemetry and engineering audits show how each design decision affects mission readiness and success.

The project addresses the challenge by turning complex engineering trade-offs into practical, visual decisions rather than abstract concepts. This is important because it gives students a fun, interactive way to understand systems engineering, experimentation, problem-solving, compromises and physics limitations required to design a successful space mission.
details:
Project Details

Space Mission is an interactive space-engineering simulation game that allows players to design, build and fly a multi-stage rocket. Players choose components such as cockpits, scientific payloads, fuel tanks and engines, then configure staging before attempting a mission. Available objectives include reaching Low Earth Orbit, geostationary orbit, lunar orbit, or landing on the Moon to collect scientific data.

The game provides real-time engineering feedback on factors such as delta-v, thrust-to-weight ratio, vehicle mass, power, communications, science return and budget. If a design cannot complete the selected mission, the engineering audit identifies problems so the player can redesign the rocket and try again.

Benefits and intended impact

The project turns complex engineering concepts into practical, visual decisions. Instead of simply learning formulas, players can see how adding fuel increases range but also increases mass, or how adding scientific equipment improves science return while affecting cost, power and vehicle performance. The intended impact is to make STEM, systems engineering and space science more engaging and accessible through experimentation.

Technologies used

The application was developed primarily in Visual Studio Code, using JavaScript, Phaser and Vite to build the browser-based game and interactive simulation. Gemini AI was also used to support development and ideation. The project runs as a web application, so no specialist hardware is required.

Creativity and design considerations

The creative element is combining a rocket-building game with an engineering simulation. Players are not simply trying to fly a rocket. They must make realistic trade-offs and understand why a mission succeeds or fails.

Key factors considered include:

  • Rocket staging and component selection
  • Engine thrust and efficiency
  • Fuel capacity and vehicle mass
  • Payload and scientific objectives
  • Mission delta-v requirements
  • Power and communications
  • Crew and recovery requirements
  • Budget limitations
  • Mission destination and trajectory
  • Scientific data collection
  • Launch readiness and mission risk

This creates an environment where failure is part of learning: players can test a design, identify deficiencies, modify the spacecraft, and immediately see how those engineering choices affect the next mission attempt.
